minutes_text:
CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 North Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Video Teleconference
  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / Small Business Assistance Task Force
  Committee Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Tuesday, May 15, 2024
  3:00 PM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  May 15, 2024 / 3:00 PM
IN ATTENDANCE:  Vice Mayor Sharona Nazarian, Councilmember Craig Corman, Deputy City
  Manager Keith Sterling, Community Outreach Manager Magdalena Davis,
  Deputy Director of Public Works Michael Hensley, Community
  Development Senior Planner Cloe Chen, Beverly Hills Chamber of
  Commerce President & CEO Todd Johnson, Chamber Director of
  Economic & Government Affairs Brittany Ganson, Chamber of Commerce
  Government Affairs Consultant Ted Green

  1) Public Comment:

  None

  2) Welcome, Introductions and Purpose of the Task Force:
  a. Larry Johnson: Program Lead Advisor at El Camino College Small Business
  Development Center
  b. Barry Axelrod: Beverly Hills Cookies
  c. Tiffany Davis: Key Entertainment
  d. Shawn Saeedian: Beverly Hills Market

  3) AskBH: Customer Relations Program:
  a. Presentation by Michael Hensley:
  i. Provides a single point of contact for all non-emergency services.
  ii. Designed to be a centralized city helpline.
  iii. If they are unable to assist a caller, they know who to transfer them to who
  can.
  iv. The number is (310) 285-1000

  4) Recommendation From Planning Commission on Portable Signage in the Public
  Right-Of-Way:
  a. Presentation by Chole Chen:
 Highlights for May 15, 2024
Small Business Assistance Task Force Committee

  i. During the temporary OpenBH program portable signs were allowed to help
  with visibility. When OpenBH was codified, there was no review of signage
  and so the question of whether to permanently allow portable signage
  remains.
  ii. The Planning Commission discussed this issue at a meeting on May 9th
  and decided that due to their importance to small businesses they would
  like to continue allowing portable signs, but in a manner that is appropriate
  for Beverly Hills. They also considered implementing a signage pilot
  program.
  iii. The Commission directed staff to create an ad hoc committee to develop
  standards and regulations with consultation from the business community
  and to return to the commission with a draft ordinance.
  b.  There will be multiple meetings that will be held for the drafting of the ordinance
  that will be open to the public.
  c.  While the ban on portable signage remains in effect, it is not currently being
  enforced.
  d.  The petition for the city to consider allowing portable signage reached over 100
  signatures when it was submitted in December.
  e.  Barry Axelrod placed a portable sign in front of his business two months ago and
  his business increased by 25%.

  5) Information Sharing & Discussion by Small Business Task Force:
  a. Shawn Saeedian stated that business was going well for him and that his foot
  traffic has increased.
  b. Barry Axelrod stated that some of his neighbors are interested in expanding their
  operating hours from 9:00 PM to 11:00 PM. He also wants to put together a
  beautification committee to improve the appearance of vacant lots in the triangle.
  He also is in favor of a city kiosk for the triangle.
  c. Larry Johnson mentioning that there will be a chamber meeting concerning
  business ADA compliance tomorrow and how business can improve access and
  avoid lawsuits.
  d. Leasing activity remains hot in the triangle, particularly for food and wellness
  businesses.
  e. Most Fashon tenants want to be in the triangle, and those that are priced out of
  Rodeo Dr typically move to North Beverly Dr, or other areas in the triangle.
  f. The area on Brighton Way between Beverly Drive and Camden is more desirable
  than the 400 block of North Beverly.
  g. Vice Mayor Nazarian likes the idea of a kiosk and a beautification committee.

  6) Future Agenda Items Discussion:
  a. Potential revitalization of La Cienega/Wilshire area.
 Highlights for May 15, 2024
Small Business Assistance Task Force Committee

  7) Adjournment:
  Date / Time: May 15, 2024 / 3:44 PM
